account:
It is day 0, just after ten, and I am still in the town hall office, due at the plaza for my market walk. I read today's appointments and returned the book to its chest. The secretary reports no correspondence, unusual news, or recorded repair requests. So far I have seen no evidence of secret activity or anything distinctly unusual in town; my feeling that something is happening without me remains only a suspicion.

The builder came to arrange this week's repairs and asked for locations, priorities, and an agreed budget before starting. I requested an inspection of the bridge and public lighting, with defects and an itemized estimate before repairs. This appears to be ordinary town maintenance, not evidence of another purpose. No paid work or spending has been authorized. My last clarification about inspection fees and bringing an estimate to accounts at one was heard only by the secretary, so I cannot assume the builder received it.

The secretary is helping keep the schedule and proposed repair arrangements recorded. Three townsfolk are visible near the town hall, but I have heard nothing from them and have no basis for assigning them any involvement. I should keep my appointments and learn what residents have actually seen or heard rather than treat ordinary activity as suspicious.
